correctness.rationale: Unique-earlier-opposite-neighbor criterion for unfilled 1-dimensional graph reduces every filtration to arrows toward the first vertex of the opposite part. With first a0,b0, all arrows are in one full star or one of two explicit flaps. Every listed star/flap is realized by an order. Mixed faces in a flap with at least two vertices have a unique flap; descending-cardinality pivot pairs are free elementary collapses, leaving one bridge per flap and the contractible pairwise-disjoint stars. Quotienting the stars yields the connected multigraph 2K_{m,n}, hence beta1=2mn-(m+n)+1 and the claimed wedge. Independent explicit enumeration and actual free-face checks at (2,2),(2,3),(3,3) reproduced 20,47,96 total faces and 8,12,18 bridge edges; these samples corroborate, not replace, the all-parameter symbolic argument.
residual_risks: The theorem is for full strong filtration complex and unfilled 1-dimensional K_mn only; it does not classify the ordinary or pure strong complex.

value.rationale: A natural uniform two-parameter integral homotopy classification and explicit collapse model, despite large original simplicial dimension; it extends beyond thin-side m=2 and can be used to understand this newly defined complex for every complete bipartite graph.
residual_risks: Classification is new only if not already implied by an inaccessible broader theorem; mathematical motivation does not itself establish priority.

final_claim: For every m,n>=2, the full strong discrete-Morse matching complex of the unfilled complete bipartite graph K_{m,n} is homotopy equivalent over the integers to a wedge of 2mn-m-n+1 circles, via an explicit collapse onto m+n disjoint star simplices joined by 2mn bridges.
limitations: The theorem is for full strong filtration complex and unfilled 1-dimensional K_mn only; it does not classify the ordinary or pure strong complex.
